column5: current_note
Host lifecycle, hello, and macOS/Windows/Linux no-flag app sessions are implemented; full named-role and privileged dispatch remain absent.

WKWebView, WebView2, and WebKitGTK backends plus the common verified profile foundation exist; Windows signed-package identity and profile lifecycle checks have real-device evidence. A same-origin five-store isolation matrix passes across signed apps and publishers and an existing second ordinary user, including restart, first-user retention, and cleanup. Full Windows profile acceptance, macOS/Linux authenticated producers and persistent stores, the destination engine policy, and the renderer bridge remain incomplete.
kipc framing, codecs, HELLO authentication, Unix bootstrap, and the Windows named-pipe app-link are implemented; channel registry and shared-memory lanes are absent.

Manifest parsing, evaluation, verified startup loading, and guard-before-handler dispatch exist, as does the single KEL-135 Windows Authenticode verifier (KEL-270 T4d S8; keld-core calls it, and its payload read-back stays with KEL-254 T3 Part B and S9); generated grants and audit logging remain target behavior.

The retained filesystem broker is implemented with verified-snapshot binding, guard-selected retained scopes, bounded no-follow traversal and regular-file I/O. Native Windows and Linux rows on exact landed ancestor `d22e454...` are publicly reported in [PR #262](https://github.com/gyldlab/keld/pull/262), while the final three-OS terminal artifact is authenticated in private Linear only and therefore is not yet a public proof surface. No production host caller is wired, and the other planned native services are absent.

Single-child supervision, crash accounting, macOS guardians, Windows primary generations, and Linux strict preparation for the no-flag primary exist; full named-role and remaining product strict admission remain absent.

Windows x64 fixed-NTFS packages support actual-SYSTEM machine-baseline initialization/admission, an explicit-UAC MachineUacDirect baseline initializer (an elevated operator run seeds the common baseline and a filtered token refuses before any write), and a native PerUserDirect baseline/bootstrap primitive under the installing user's owner-private profile. The per-user initializer seeds a verified immutable baseline, stable activation lease, floor/current/LKG and provenance-last commit. Ordinary-token no-UAC, real LPAC mutation denial and 11 baseline crash cuts pass. Native Windows updater tests also prove higher-release extraction and completion of an immutable stage under the retained writer lease; the completed stage is neither published nor selected and active records/journal stay unchanged. KEL-270 T4b adds the common journaled PerUserDirect transaction: activation, exact receipt binding, commit/rollback, version retirement, recovery from every persisted cut (62 native crash cuts) and the explicit unjournaled-version repair for orphans left by the earlier order. KEL-270 F1 journals each attempt before renaming its stage to the version name, re-verifies the candidate before the floor moves and abandons an attempt whose stage is gone. KEL-270 F3a adds read-only active package selection for ordinary startup (KEL-254 AC4): a shared-lease snapshot that refuses a pending journal as journal-bound and a lease sharing conflict as WriterActive, requires current to be a known-good artifact within the floor, admits only referenced versions with metadata admission and the signed no-migration package policy, and pins the selected tree and its protected ancestry; 15 native tests and 7 mutation controls. KEL-270 F3b adds the startup repair: an absent or undecodable current is republished from a re-validated last-known-good under the PerUserDirect writer lease (6 mutation controls); a decoded current is never rewritten. KEL-254 T2b adds executable-located selection: the build-time ExpectedAppIdentity is decoded and matched field-exactly against the located provenance record before that same handle is admitted against the recorded mode's profile; every recorded root must be the located root by volume serial and file ID on the record's volume, the executable handle must be the selected tree's keld-host.exe, and current is repaired only for the last-known-good host (12 native per-user tests and an independent security review); machine-mode and non-NTFS selector cells remain operator rows. KEL-254 T3 Part B adds ExpectedAppIdentity::from_signed_image, which reads the embedded expectation through keld-pack's handle reader from the image KEL-135 just verified and applies decode's channel and key admission (container and read refusals are KELD-UPDATE-019; payload refusals stay KELD-UPDATE-017); the KEL-96 host now consumes executable-located selection. Candidate selection, installer integration, host candidate launch and 30-second health, feed orchestration and the machine modes remain absent.

Windows hosts can stream canonical Windows v0 tar/zstd update packages with the fixed no-migration policy and byte-domain size/BLAKE3 receipts; other hosts refuse production before I/O. It also owns the canonical build-time ExpectedAppIdentity payload codec (KEL-254 T2b): a domain-tagged app id, channel, target and Ed25519 update key with fixed bounds, no control characters and exact EOF, pinned by a golden vector; KEL-19 T1 adds the host container (#386): a pure writer embeds the payload as a dedicated `.keldeai` PE section of the unsigned host before its final signature, and a positioned-read reader over a byte slice (every target) or an open Windows file handle shares one stack-bounded structure parser; the reader authenticates nothing, so a result is authentic only when read from the handle KEL-135 has just verified. The KEL-254 T3 Part B host consumer reads the container at boot through keld-update's from_signed_image; KEL-19 T2 (signed coverage) and T3 (`keld build` integration) remain absent. Installers, signing, notarization, CLI build integration and cross-host assembly remain absent.
Compatibility evidence types, scoring, and lifecycle conformance exist; broad Electron host emulation is absent.
The shipping host owns hello and macOS/Windows/Linux no-flag sessions; the destination registry and release packaging remain absent.
create emits the checked-in Rust-derived echo payload declarations; dev, doctor, MCP, hello, and IPC diagnostics exist, while build, migrate, gen, and ext remain reserved.
The Electron facade implements lifecycle and the app-link client; the wider Electron module surface is absent.
The canonical TypeScript app-link transport is live, and bounded cold tooling derives checked-in echo payload declarations from the Rust structs; general schema codegen and bulk lanes remain absent.
The typed SDK for supervised Bun roles is specified but no package is tracked.
The renderer bridge and polyfill package are specified but no package is tracked.
The npm binary resolver is specified but no package is tracked.
The contract-definition and code-generation package is specified but no package is tracked.
The package-manager scaffolding entrypoint is specified but no package is tracked.
The tracked workspace, architecture, agent workflow, and CI exist; the first attributed performance harness remains absent.
macOS, Windows, and Linux no-flag app sessions exist; the full public role API and release artifact chain remain absent.
MCP v1, permission evaluation, guard dispatch, one filesystem broker, and bounded echo declaration generation exist; bulk IPC, general schema codegen, and broad compatibility remain absent.
The Linux strict mechanism is implemented and consumed by the no-flag primary; distribution, signed updates, remaining OS/profile admission, limits, reporting, and addon workers remain incomplete.
Compatibility-depth, corpus, pinned-engine, and stable-plugin goals are specified but not implemented.

The shipping app-link uses a current-user protected named pipe plus HELLO; distinct ordinary-user denial and authorized same-user successor echo are proven, while decimal diagnostic compatibility remains.
The no-flag host, native window, app link, recovery, and ordered cleanup are implemented for the current slice.

The no-flag host, native window, named-pipe app link, recovery, ordered cleanup, and authenticated Authenticode identity-to-persistent-WebView2 wiring are implemented; the single KEL-135 Windows Authenticode verifier is owned by keld-guard (KEL-270 T4d S8) and keld-core calls it. Windows admits two boot states (KEL-254 A3 AC2): a dev lease reaches only the owner-private dev-stage validator, and a lease-less launch boots only the authenticated installed package (KEL-254 T3 Part B). keld-core verifies the executable once, reads its embedded ExpectedAppIdentity from that pinned handle (KELD-UPDATE-019/017), selects the installation through KEL-53's executable-located entrypoint (KELD-UPDATE-*), requires the protected record's publisher and app id to equal the verified identity (KELD-WV-009) and opens the strict boot files beneath the selected tree, all before any listener, child or window; the persistent profile comes from that boot identity. On 2026-10-06 the KEL-135 signed rows passed on fresh per-run PerUserDirect installations of P1/P2-signed embedded hosts (RAMANI, unelevated): startup, profile concurrency, crash release, the five-store App A/B/other-publisher isolation matrix and both purge rows, with signed refusals for a host without a container, one outside an installation, one under another recorded publisher and one signed for another app. The second ordinary user's row, machine-mode installed cells and updated, rolled-back or candidate boot (KEL-254 T4) remain unrun. Earlier dev-stage evidence covers the second ordinary user's store isolation, restart, cleanup, and first-user retention; filesystem denial; and saved-media grant revocation. Broader Windows profile acceptance and all macOS/Linux browser-profile acceptance remain incomplete.

The no-flag host, WebKitGTK window, authenticated app link, strict Bun generations, recovery, CLI/host-death cleanup, and relaunch are implemented for Ubuntu/Debian x86_64 Wayland; X11, non-Debian, and release packaging remain unverified.
